title: Improve quantized inference kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant and dequant-fusion paths
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context and motivation: Production inference at Redwood increasingly needs efficient low-precision kernels to reduce unit cost and keep tail latencies low. This PR implements a suite of quantized kernel improvements targeting INT8 and experimental FP8 paths, a smoothquant per-layer scaling pass to stabilize asymmetric quantization, and a dequant-fusion execution path that collapses dequant->compute->requant sequences in critical attention and MLP kernels. Together these changes improve throughput and reduce per-token compute overhead while keeping numerical regressions within validated thresholds.

What this PR does (high level): added a smoothquant pre-processing pass that computes per-channel scale factors and optional bias folding; implemented a fused dequant+matmul+requant CUDA kernel for attention and feed-forward blocks; added FP8 storage path with runtime selection and fallback to INT8/FP16; introduced kernel selection logic in the runtime to prefer dequant-fusion when model layout and device support match; added microbenchmarks and CI perf harness; added runtime flags and feature gates (enable_smoothquant, enable_dequant_fusion, preferred_precision_order).

Benchmarks (summaries): microbenchmarks on A100 and H100: INT8 dequant-fusion path improves end-to-end token throughput by ~1.7-1.9x for decoder-only LLMs at 2048 context vs baseline INT8 with separate dequant; FP8 path yields ~1.25-1.4x improvement over INT8 on layers dominated by GEMM when using FP8 storage + FP16 compute; smoothquant reduced per-layer activation clipping and improved 99th percentile latency by ~20-30% in stress tests. End-to-end RLHF-style batch generation workloads saw ~22% cost reduction in our internal cost model when using the new default precision order [INT8_FUSED, FP8, FP16]. All numbers include KV cache and continuous batching enabled.

Compatibility and safety: the kernels are opt-in via flags and runtime will automatically fall back to existing stable paths if FP8 support is absent or if numerical checks (small validation set) fail. We preserve model artifacts: smoothquant writes an ancillary per-layer scale table but we support a compatibility mode that embeds scales into weight tensors for customers that prefer no sidecar metadata. We added unit and numerical regression tests to cover small GPT-like models and a subset of the eval harness.

Files changed (high level): redwood/runtime/kernels/quant/dequant_fusion.cu, redwood/runtime/kernels/quant/fp8_kernels.cu, redwood/runtime/kernels/quant/smoothquant_pass.cpp, redwood/runtime/selection/precision_selector.cpp, redwood/runtime/scheduler/batching_policy.cpp (add hooks to prefer fused paths), tests/perf/bench_quantized.py, tests/unit/test_smoothquant.py, docs/quantization.md, ci/perf-workflows/quant-bench.yml and small changes to build scripts and cmake.

Testing and CI: full CI passed on linux-aarch64 and linux-x86_64 CUDA 12.1 images. Perf CI run passed against baseline for release branch; there was one initial regression in a specific H100 driver combo which we fixed by tightening FP8 rounding path and re-ran (CI rerun logged). Integration tests with Dedicated infra were exercised on a smaller staging pool. We also ran a private canary rollout on a small subset of customers (opt-in) to validate end-to-end integrations.

Reviewer notes and trade-offs: dequant-fusion reduces kernel launch overhead but increases kernel complexity and register pressure; we guard it behind device capability checks and a runtime heuristic that measures occupancy. FP8 storage reduces memory bandwidth but requires careful rounding/accumulation to avoid divergence in logits; we intentionally keep FP16 accumulation in many critical paths and expose a precision order preference. Smoothquant introduces a per-layer calibration step which adds a small one-time preprocessing cost during model load; this is amortized for long-lived endpoints.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind default feature flags off. We will enable enable_dequant_fusion for internal canaries and Dedicated reservations for customers who opt-in. After 2 weeks of canary telemetry and no regressions we'll flip the default for new hosted model uploads and provide migration tooling for existing models.

Related: builds on ENG-4821 (quant kernels design doc) and is paired with a follow-up PR that exposes quantization tuning controls in the Console (planned ENG-4873).

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4821), [x] unit tests added, [x] perf benches added and CI harnessed, [x] feature flags implemented, [x] docs updated.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main.

Notes: The description above is intentionally compact; see individual commits and tests for full diffs and microbench harness outputs.

release_notes: Improved quantized inference kernels: added smoothquant, dequant-fusion kernels, and FP8 storage path. Expect reduced per-token cost and improved throughput for quantized deployments. Feature gated; rollout staged via canaries.
